claim_title: True paired-acquisition structure is required for tissue/category preservation and downstream transfer
claim_text_safe: Training paired-acquisition factorization with true same-region cross-scanner pairs produces substantially better biological-branch tissue-identity preservation and category-retrieval performance than any broken-pair or random-pair control. Scanner suppression persists across all pairing conditions, but tissue-identity preservation degrades monotonically as the biological correspondence in the positive pair is weakened. The biological correspondence — not scanner balancing alone — is the active ingredient.
strongest_evidence: Pair-structure boundary test (e4819c42): In SCORPION DINOv2, true same-region paired cosine = 0.8796, top-1 retrieval = 0.9999 vs same-slide-different-region = 0.8089, shuffled-sample = 0.7668, random = 0.7247. In canine SCC DINOv2, true-pair paired cosine = 0.7300, retrieval = 0.9334 vs non-true band 0.5422–0.5849. Scanner suppression is maintained across all conditions (bio scanner probe 0.36–0.41), but tissue identity degrades with looser pairing.
strongest_baseline: True same-region pairs (L0) in the pairing ladder. Scanner-balanced random pairing (L3) performs no better than fully random (L4).
limitation: The pairing ladder only controls pair construction, not training dynamics. All conditions use the same architecture and losses. Cross-backbone evidence extends to SCORPION DINOv2/Phikon/ResNet50 but uses pair/tissue retrieval metrics, not category labels — SCORPION lacks biological category annotations.
forbidden_overclaim: Paired-acquisition requires exactly same-region pairs (same-slide-different-region still preserves substantial tissue identity). Any broken-pair setup destroys the method (scanner suppression is maintained across all conditions). True pairs are necessary for scanner suppression (false; scanner adversary works regardless of pair quality).
figure_or_table_candidate: Pairing ladder table showing paired cosine/top-1 retrieval/scanner probe for each level across both datasets
reviewer_objection_answered: Scanner balancing across the batch isn't sufficient — scanner-balanced random pairing (L3) performs similarly to fully random (L4) and substantially below true same-region pairs (L0). Same-slide-different-region (L1) is measurably below true same-region (L0) in both datasets.
remaining_objection: Cannot disentangle whether degradation comes from weaker biological correspondence, weaker scanner correspondence, or both. Same-slide-different-region pairs change both the biological and scanner content simultaneously.

claim_title: Paired-acquisition produces measurable branch separation: biological branch suppresses scanner signal while preserving tissue/category structure; acquisition branch captures scanner signal
claim_text_safe: Under true-pair training, the biological branch substantially reduces scanner recoverability (scanner probe 0.8656 → 0.3610 in canine SCC DINOv2) while preserving tissue-category structure (category probe 0.4068 → 0.3855, Δ = −0.0213; neighborhood purity improves from 0.9542 → 0.9729). The acquisition branch retains scanner signal (scanner probe 0.8620) while category structure is reduced (category probe 0.3458, purity 0.5295). Cross-covariance between branches is low (RMS < 0.10).
strongest_evidence: Biological label preservation audit (bec06eb4): true_pair_biological achieves category/scanner ratio 1.07 (vs original 0.47), scanner suppression δ = +0.5046, category preservation δ = −0.0213. true_pair_acquisition scanner capture 0.8620 with category leakage 0.3456. Biological purity K1 = 0.9729 vs acquisition 0.5295.
strongest_baseline: Original frozen DINOv2 features (pre-factorization state). Shuffled-sample biological branch (shows broken-pair factorization cannot achieve same separation).
limitation: Branch separation is measured via linear probe accuracies and neighborhood purity — diagnostic metrics, not proof of complete information-theoretic independence. Cross-covariance is low but nonzero. Separation is partial, not perfect. All evidence is from canine SCC DINOv2 only; SCORPION lacks category labels.
forbidden_overclaim: Perfect disentanglement or complete separation (separation is partial; residual leakage exists in both branches). The biological branch is scanner-free (scanner probe 0.3610, well above chance 0.20). The acquisition branch is category-free (category probe 0.3456, substantially above baseline).
figure_or_table_candidate: Two-panel figure: (a) scanner probe vs category probe scatter, (b) biological vs acquisition branch purity bar chart. Central result table.
reviewer_objection_answered: PCA at k=32 is worse: scanner probe 0.6489 and category probe 0.2893. PCA increases effective rank; factorization reduces it in both branches. PCA is blind to scanner/category distinction.
remaining_objection: No information-theoretic independence metric exists in the evidence stack. All separation metrics are probe-based and may not detect higher-order dependencies.

claim_title: Oldstyle centroid/QR linear projection is the strongest raw scanner-removal baseline; paired-acquisition should not be framed as best-in-class scanner erasure
claim_text_safe: Oldstyle centroid/QR linear projection (oldstyle_keep_k4) achieves scanner probe accuracy at chance level (0.2000) while preserving category accuracy (0.4004) — strictly better raw scanner removal and category preservation than true_pair_biological (scanner 0.3614, category 0.3860). The paired-acquisition contribution is not raw scanner erasure but structured separation: an explicit scanner-bearing acquisition branch (scanner capture 0.8651) with biological leakage that can be reduced by bottlenecking.
strongest_evidence: Oldstyle residual branch separation audit (3450ede2): oldstyle_keep_k4 scanner probe 0.2000, category probe 0.4004 vs true_pair_biological scanner probe 0.3614, category probe 0.3860. Linear baseline consistency audit (a325c009): documents why oldstyle (centroid/QR) is stronger than newstyle (logistic-SVD, scanner 0.7071).
strongest_baseline: oldstyle_keep_k4 (centroid/QR) — the reference baseline that paired-acquisition must be measured against in all scanner-removal comparisons.
limitation: The oldstyle baseline is a post-hoc linear operation on frozen DINOv2 embeddings. It does not produce an explicit acquisition branch, cannot be inspected, and cannot be used for acquisition swapping. It is strong at blind removal but provides no structural decomposition.
forbidden_overclaim: Paired-acquisition removes scanner bias better than any linear method (false; oldstyle_keep_k4 wins). Paired-acquisition is the best scanner-removal approach. Paired-acquisition beats all baselines on scanner removal. Any text omitting the oldstyle baseline when discussing scanner-removal strength.
figure_or_table_candidate: Scoreboard-style summary table showing scanner probe/category probe/scanner-capture for oldstyle_keep_k4/true_pair_biological/true_pair_acquisition/bottlenecked variants
reviewer_objection_answered: If you only want scanner removal, use oldstyle_keep_k4. If you want to inspect, bottleneck, or swap the acquisition factor, use paired-acquisition. We started with a weaker logistic-SVD baseline, found the discrepancy, and upgraded to the stronger centroid/QR baseline.
remaining_objection: A nonlinear scanner-removal baseline (e.g. adversarial feature projection) could be even stronger than oldstyle centroid/QR. We have not tested this.

claim_title: Bottlenecking the acquisition branch improves the separation frontier by reducing acquisition-branch biological leakage while preserving scanner capture and biological downstream transfer
claim_text_safe: Reducing the acquisition branch capacity from 64D (true_pair) to 8D or 16D with stronger cross-covariance regularization substantially reduces biological/tissue leakage in the acquisition branch. In canine SCC DINOv2, acq_dim8_default reduces acquisition-branch category probe from 0.3456 (true_pair) to 0.1598 (δ = −0.1858) while maintaining scanner capture (0.8643 vs 0.8651). In SCORPION DINOv2, acquisition-branch tissue-retrieval leakage drops from 0.0944 to 0.0231, with similar improvements in Phikon (0.0739 → 0.0204) and ResNet50 (0.1705 → 0.0505).
strongest_evidence: Acquisition bottleneck separation frontier sweep (a89bfb32): acq_dim8_default acq category 0.1598 (vs true_pair 0.3456) with preserved scanner capture 0.8643. Cross-backbone validation (0e2af247): SCORPION acq_dim8 retrieval leakage 0.0231 vs true_pair 0.0944 (DINOv2), 0.0204 vs 0.0739 (Phikon), 0.0505 vs 0.1705 (ResNet50).
strongest_baseline: true_pair_acquisition (64D, no bottleneck) — the pre-bottleneck acquisition branch.
limitation: Only 2 dimensions (8, 16) with 2 regularization strengths tested at full scale. Frontier is sparse — cannot claim continuous Pareto front or optimal bottleneck size. SCORPION evidence uses tissue-retrieval leakage, not category leakage. Very aggressive bottlenecking (dim < 8) not tested.
forbidden_overclaim: Bottlenecking eliminates biological leakage (acq_dim8_default still has category probe 0.1598). The bottleneck is optimal at dimension 8 (true optimum unknown). Bottlenecking solves the separation problem (residual leakage remains). SCORPION bottleneck reduces category leakage (SCORPION has no category labels; it reduces tissue/pair-retrieval leakage).
figure_or_table_candidate: Frontier plot: acquisition-branch category leakage vs scanner capture. Three-panel cross-backbone figure: SCORPION DINOv2/Phikon/ResNet50 with tissue-retrieval leakage bars.
reviewer_objection_answered: Scanner capture is preserved (0.8643 vs 0.8651) while category leakage drops (0.3456 → 0.1598). The bottleneck selectively constrains biological information because scanner-discriminative information requires lower capacity. Cross-backbone validation across three SCORPION backbones confirms generalization.
remaining_objection: Cannot isolate bottleneck-dimension effect from regularization-strength effect with only two selected variants. No direct causal evidence that capacity reduction alone drives the improvement.

claim_title: Decoder-based acquisition swapping supports factor-like behavior; bottlenecking improves biological/category preservation under swapped acquisition factors
claim_text_safe: When the acquisition branch from one sample is combined with the biological branch from another sample via the learned decoder, scanner identity follows the acquisition branch: scanner follow rate averages 0.855 across all variants and swap types. Category preservation averages ~0.40. Branch-space NN purity: bio-space K1 category purity 0.980; acq-space K1 scanner purity 0.880. Decoder-reconstructed features show scanner-follow behavior (0.806 average, 0.901 for same-sample/different-scanner swaps) and category preservation (0.978 for bottlenecked variants). This is factor-like behavior — scanner information follows the acquisition branch through recombination — but does not prove perfect causal factorization.
strongest_evidence: Acquisition factor swapping audit (aa8d0596): scanner follow rate 0.855 across all variants/swap types. Bottleneck variants show lower acq_category_leakage under swap. Decoder-space scanner follow 0.806 overall (0.901 for same-sample swap). Bio-space K1 category purity 0.980 vs acq-space K1 scanner purity 0.880.
strongest_baseline: true_pair (64D, no bottleneck) — baseline acquisition branch against which bottlenecked-swap improvements are measured. Same-sample/different-scanner swap (Type A) is the strongest test case.
limitation: Single-dataset evidence (canine SCC DINOv2 only). No SCORPION or cross-backbone swapping. NN scanner purity (0.880) weaker than NN category purity (0.980). Decoder trained for reconstruction, not factor manipulation — recombination artifacts may exist. Only three variant configurations tested. Swap is at feature-representation level, not image-pixel level.
forbidden_overclaim: Proves perfect causal acquisition factor (factor-like behavior only; NN scanner purity 0.880, not 1.0). Proves biological and acquisition factors are independent (category preservation under swap ~0.40). Enables acquisition factor editing for deployment (research audit only). Scanner information is fully encoded in the acquisition branch (bio_scanner_leakage remains 0.032–0.213). Works across all scanners and domains (single dataset, 5 scanners).
figure_or_table_candidate: Swap-type diagram. Bar chart: scanner follow rate and category preservation rate by variant and swap type. Table: branch-space NN purity by variant and swap type.
reviewer_objection_answered: The decoder-space scanner follow rate (0.806–0.901) supports factor-like recombination beyond simple discriminative residual. The swap test uses held-out test samples; same-sample/different-scanner swap (Type A) keeps biological content identical and only changes the acquisition branch.
remaining_objection: Nearest-neighbor scanner purity in acquisition space (0.880) is weaker than category purity in biological space (0.980). The acquisition branch carries scanner information but it does not dominate the branch's neighborhood structure to the same degree. No cross-dataset or cross-backbone swap evidence.
